exercises.title: Bài 1 · Pets and farm animals
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Veterinarians work with many kinds of animals. Some treat small animals, such as dogs, cats and rabbits. These are usually pets, and their owners often think of them as members of the family. Other vets work with large animals, such as horses, cattle and pigs. Farm animals that are kept for milk, meat or eggs are called livestock, and chickens and ducks are called poultry.

All vertebrates have a similar basic body plan. The skeleton supports the body and protects organs: the skull protects the brain, and the ribs protect the heart and lungs. Dogs and cats walk on paws and have claws, while horses and cattle have hooves. The skin and the coat protect the body from cold, heat and injury.

The internal organs are also similar. The heart pumps blood, the lungs bring in oxygen, and the stomach and intestines digest food. The liver cleans the blood, and the kidneys remove waste. Because the anatomy is similar, it is easy to forget that a vet must still know the differences between species. For example, a horse cannot vomit, but a dog can.

content.q: Livestock are kept for milk, meat or eggs.
content.why: Đoạn 1: vật nuôi lấy sữa, thịt hoặc trứng gọi là livestock.

content.q: Dogs and horses both have hooves.
content.why: Đoạn 2: chó, mèo có bàn chân và móng vuốt; ngựa, bò có móng guốc.

content.q: The ribs protect the heart and lungs.
content.why: Đoạn 2: xương sườn bảo vệ tim và phổi.

content.q: A horse can vomit easily.
content.why: Đoạn 3: ngựa không thể nôn, còn chó thì có thể.

content.q: What do the lungs do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: phổi đưa oxy vào cơ thể.

content.q: What does the skull protect?
content.why: Đoạn 2: hộp sọ bảo vệ não.

content.q: What is poultry?
content.why: Đoạn 1: gà và vịt gọi là gia cầm.

content.q: Why must a vet know the differences between species?
content.why: Đoạn 3: cấu tạo tương tự nhưng mỗi loài có khác biệt, ví dụ ngựa không nôn được.
opts: All animals are exactly the same.
Their anatomy is similar but not the same.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · A busy morning at the clinic
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
The clinic opens at eight. The first patient is a puppy called Bun, who is coming for his first vaccination. The vet weighs him, listens to his heart and checks his coat and skin. His owner asks many questions about feeding and training.

Next comes an old cat with a limp. The veterinary nurse holds the cat gently while the vet checks each paw. She finds a small cut under one claw. The nurse cleans it and puts on a light bandage.

At ten o'clock, the vet leaves for a farm visit. A farmer is worried about one of his calves, which is not drinking milk. The vet takes the calf's temperature and examines its stomach. While she is working, the farmer's wife is preparing a warm place for the calf to rest. Back at the clinic in the afternoon, the vet writes her notes, and the nurse sterilises the instruments for the next day.

content.q: Bun comes to the clinic for his first vaccination.
content.why: Đoạn 1: Bun đến để tiêm vaccine lần đầu.

content.q: The old cat has a limp because of a broken leg.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bác sĩ tìm thấy vết cắt nhỏ dưới móng, không phải gãy chân.

content.q: A calf on the farm is not drinking milk.
content.why: Đoạn 3: người nông dân lo vì con bê không bú sữa.

content.q: The vet goes to the farm in the afternoon.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cô đến trang trại lúc mười giờ sáng.

content.q: What does the vet do with the puppy?
content.why: Đoạn 1: cân, nghe tim, kiểm tra lông và da.
opts: She weighs him and listens to his heart.

content.q: What does the nurse do with the cut on the cat's paw?
content.why: Đoạn 2: y tá làm sạch và băng nhẹ.
opts: She cleans it and puts on a bandage.

content.q: What is wrong with the calf?
What does the nurse do at the end of the day?
content.why: Đoạn 3: y tá tiệt trùng dụng cụ cho ngày hôm sau.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Taking a history
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Before the examination, the vet always talks to the owner. This conversation is called taking the history, and it often gives the most important clues. The vet asks about the animal's age, diet, vaccinations and behaviour. Most importantly, she asks about the problem: When did it start? Is the animal eating and drinking normally? Has there been any vomiting or diarrhoea?

Mrs Lan brings her dog, Rex, to the clinic. He has been lethargic for two days and he has not eaten since Monday. He vomited twice yesterday. The vet takes his temperature: it is 39.9 °C, which is higher than normal. She also finds that Rex is slightly dehydrated.

The vet recommends a blood test and an ultrasound. The results show an infection in the intestine. Rex stays in the clinic for a day and receives fluids through a drip and an antibiotic. By the next evening, he is walking more actively and he is hungry again. The vet gives Mrs Lan instructions for feeding him at home.

content.q: The history often gives the most important clues.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cuộc trò chuyện với chủ thường cho gợi ý quan trọng nhất.

content.q: Rex has eaten normally this week.
content.why: Đoạn 2: Rex không ăn từ thứ Hai.

content.q: Rex's temperature was higher than normal.

content.why: Đoạn 3: Rex ở lại phòng khám một ngày.

content.q: Which question belongs to taking a history?
content.why: Đoạn 1: vet hỏi khi nào vấn đề bắt đầu.

content.q: What do the tests show?

content.why: Đoạn 3: truyền dịch qua đường tĩnh mạch.

content.q: What happens by the next evening?
content.why: Đoạn 3: Rex đi lại hoạt bát hơn và đã đói.
opts: Rex is more active and hungry.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · The physical examination
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
A complete physical examination follows a clear order. First, the vet looks at the animal from a distance. She watches how it stands, walks and breathes. Is it alert, or is it lethargic? Then she examines the body from nose to tail.

She starts with the head: eyes, ears, nose and mouth. The colour of the gums is important because pale gums can show blood loss. Next, she listens to the heart and lungs with a stethoscope, a method called auscultation. She counts the heart rate and the respiratory rate and feels the pulse. After that, she uses palpation to feel the abdomen, the lymph nodes and the joints. Finally, she measures the temperature with a thermometer and weighs the animal.

Every finding is written in the medical record. If the vet notices a problem, she may recommend more tests, such as a blood test, an X-ray or an ultrasound. A careful examination takes only ten minutes, but it can save a life.

content.q: The vet starts by looking at the animal from a distance.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bắt đầu bằng quan sát từ xa.

content.q: Pale gums can show blood loss.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nướu nhợt có thể báo hiệu mất máu.

content.q: Auscultation means feeling the abdomen with the hands.
content.why: Đoạn 2: auscultation là nghe tim phổi; sờ bụng là palpation.

content.q: A careful examination takes about two hours.
content.why: Đoạn 3: chỉ mất khoảng mười phút.

content.q: What does the vet do with a stethoscope?
content.why: Đoạn 2: nghe tim và phổi gọi là auscultation.
opts: She listens to the heart and lungs.

content.q: What is palpation used for?
content.why: Đoạn 2: sờ nắn bụng, hạch bạch huyết và khớp.
opts: Feeling the abdomen, lymph nodes and joints

content.q: Where are all the findings written?
content.why: Đoạn 3: mọi phát hiện ghi vào hồ sơ bệnh án.

content.q: Which tests may the vet recommend next?
content.why: Đoạn 3: xét nghiệm máu, X-quang hoặc siêu âm.
opts: A blood test, an X-ray or an ultrasound

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Vaccination: why it matters
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Vaccination is one of the most effective ways to protect animals from serious diseases. A vaccine contains a weak or killed virus or bacterium. When it is injected, the body makes antibodies, so it can fight the real disease later. This protection is called immunity.

Puppies and kittens receive their first vaccines at about eight weeks. A booster is given a few weeks later and then once a year or every three years, depending on the vaccine. Common vaccines protect dogs against distemper, parvovirus and rabies. Rabies vaccination is very important because the disease is almost always fatal and it can be passed to humans.

Vaccines are safe, but they can cause mild side effects, such as tiredness or a small swelling at the injection site. These effects usually disappear in a day or two. Serious reactions are very rare. If many animals in an area are vaccinated, the disease cannot spread easily. This is called herd immunity, and it also protects the animals that cannot be vaccinated.

content.q: A vaccine helps the body make antibodies.
content.why: Đoạn 1: cơ thể tạo kháng thể sau khi tiêm.

content.q: Puppies receive their first vaccines at about two years of age.
content.why: Đoạn 2: chó con tiêm mũi đầu khoảng 8 tuần tuổi.

content.q: Rabies can be passed to humans.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bệnh dại có thể lây sang người.

content.q: Serious reactions to vaccines are very common.
content.why: Đoạn 3: phản ứng nặng rất hiếm.

content.q: What is immunity?
content.why: Đoạn 1: miễn dịch là sự bảo vệ chống lại bệnh.

content.q: When is the booster given?
content.why: Đoạn 2: mũi nhắc lại sau vài tuần.
opts: A few weeks after the first vaccine

content.q: Which are mild side effects of vaccines?
content.why: Đoạn 3: mệt mỏi hoặc sưng nhẹ tại chỗ tiêm.

content.q: What does herd immunity do?
content.why: Đoạn 3: bảo vệ cả những con không thể tiêm.
opts: It also protects animals that cannot be vaccinated.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Fleas, ticks and worms
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Parasites are a common health problem in pets. External parasites live on the skin. Fleas jump from animal to animal and make them scratch. A cat with a serious flea problem can even become anaemic. Ticks attach to the skin and drink blood, and they can carry diseases. Mites cause mange, which makes the skin red and itchy.

Internal parasites live inside the body. Roundworms and tapeworms live in the intestine, and heartworm lives in the heart and blood vessels. Some of them can infect people, especially children, so owners should wash their hands after touching their pets.

The vet recommends a regular parasite control programme. Treatments include spot-on drops, tablets and collars. Puppies and kittens are dewormed every two weeks until they are twelve weeks old, and adults are treated every three months. Treatment alone is not enough. The owner should also clean the bedding, vacuum the house and treat all the animals in the family at the same time.

content.q: Fleas jump from animal to animal.
content.why: Đoạn 1: bọ chét nhảy từ vật này sang vật khác.

content.q: Heartworm lives in the intestine.
content.why: Đoạn 2: giun tim sống ở tim và mạch máu; giun tròn, sán dây ở ruột.

content.q: Some internal parasites can infect people.
content.why: Đoạn 2: một số có thể lây sang người, nhất là trẻ em.

content.q: Treatment alone is enough; cleaning is not necessary.
content.why: Đoạn 3: chủ còn phải dọn ổ, hút bụi và điều trị tất cả vật nuôi.

content.q: What can a serious flea problem cause in a cat?

content.why: Đoạn 1: ve bám vào da và hút máu.

content.why: Đoạn 3: thú trưởng thành điều trị mỗi ba tháng.

content.q: What should owners do besides treating the pet?
content.why: Đoạn 3: dọn ổ, hút bụi, điều trị cùng lúc cho mọi vật nuôi.
opts: Clean the bedding and treat all animals at the same time

exercises.title: Bài 1 · A dog with bloat
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
On Saturday night, Mr Binh called the emergency clinic. His large dog, Max, had eaten a big meal and then run in the garden. Now his stomach was swollen and he was trying to vomit without success. The vet told Mr Binh to bring Max immediately.

When they arrived, the vet did triage and saw that Max was in shock. His gums were pale and his heart rate was very high. The diagnosis was gastric dilatation and volvulus, or bloat, a life-threatening emergency. The vet started an IV drip, gave oxygen and took an X-ray. Then she moved Max to the operating theatre.

Under general anaesthesia, the vet released the gas and put the stomach back in its normal position. She also fixed it to the body wall so that the problem could not happen again. Max stayed in the clinic for three days. If Mr Binh had waited until the morning, Max would have died. Today, he is healthy again, but he eats several small meals instead of one big meal.

content.q: Max had eaten a big meal before his stomach swelled.
content.why: Đoạn 1: Max ăn một bữa lớn rồi chạy trong vườn.

content.q: Max's gums were pink and normal.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nướu nhợt và nhịp tim rất cao.

content.q: The vet fixed the stomach to the body wall.
content.why: Đoạn 3: để vấn đề không tái diễn.

content.q: Mr Binh waited until the morning to call the vet.
content.why: Đoạn 1: ông gọi ngay tối thứ Bảy.

content.q: What was the diagnosis?
content.why: Đoạn 2: giãn và xoắn dạ dày (bloat).

content.q: What did the vet start straight away?
content.why: Đoạn 2: truyền dịch, cho thở oxy, chụp X-quang.

content.q: What would have happened if Mr Binh had waited until the morning?
content.why: Đoạn 3: Max sẽ chết nếu chờ đến sáng.

content.q: How does Max eat now?

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Spaying and neutering
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Spaying is the removal of the ovaries and usually the uterus of a female animal. Neutering, or castration, is the removal of the testicles of a male. Both are among the most common operations in veterinary practice.

Before the operation, the animal must not eat for several hours. The vet gives a sedative, then inserts a catheter into a vein and gives general anaesthesia. A tube is placed in the windpipe, and a nurse monitors the heart rate, breathing and temperature during the whole operation. The skin is cleaned and the instruments are sterile. After the surgery, the vet closes the incision with sutures and gives pain relief.

At home, the owner must keep the animal quiet for about ten days. A cone stops the animal from licking the wound. The owner should check the wound every day and call the vet if it becomes red or swollen.

The operations prevent unwanted litters and reduce the risk of some diseases, such as infections of the uterus. However, the animal may gain weight more easily, so the owner may have to adjust its diet.

content.q: Spaying is performed on female animals.
content.why: Đoạn 1: spay là cắt buồng trứng, thường cả tử cung, ở con cái.

content.q: The animal can eat normally before the operation.
content.why: Đoạn 2: không được ăn trong nhiều giờ trước mổ.

content.q: A nurse monitors the animal during the surgery.
content.why: Đoạn 2: y tá theo dõi nhịp tim, hô hấp và nhiệt độ.

content.q: The cone allows the animal to lick the wound.
content.why: Đoạn 3: cone ngăn thú liếm vết mổ.

content.q: What is neutering?
content.why: Đoạn 1: neutering (castration) là cắt tinh hoàn ở con đực.
opts: The removal of the testicles of a male

content.q: What does the vet give after the surgery?
content.why: Đoạn 2: đóng vết mổ bằng chỉ khâu và cho thuốc giảm đau.

content.q: What should the owner do if the wound becomes red or swollen?
content.why: Đoạn 3: gọi bác sĩ thú y.

content.q: Why may the owner have to adjust the diet?
content.why: Đoạn 4: sau triệt sản thú dễ tăng cân.
opts: The animal may gain weight more easily.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · How a cow digests grass
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Cattle, sheep and goats are ruminants. They can digest grass and hay, which many other animals cannot use. Their secret is a stomach with four compartments. The first and largest compartment is the rumen. It contains billions of bacteria that break down plant fibre.

A cow eats quickly and swallows the food without chewing much. Later she brings it back to her mouth and chews it again. This is called chewing the cud. The food then passes through the other compartments and into the intestine, where nutrients are absorbed.

Because the rumen depends on bacteria, a sudden change of feed can be dangerous. If a cow eats too much concentrate, acid builds up in the rumen and she may become seriously ill. For this reason, farmers change the diet slowly over a week or two. A balanced ration includes forage such as grass, hay or silage, a little concentrate, and minerals and vitamins. A good diet means healthier animals and higher milk yield.

content.q: Cows have a stomach with four compartments.
The rumen is the smallest compartment.
content.why: Đoạn 1: dạ cỏ là ngăn đầu tiên và lớn nhất.

content.q: A sudden change of feed can be dangerous for a cow.
content.why: Đoạn 3: thay đổi thức ăn đột ngột có thể nguy hiểm.

content.q: A cow chews the food thoroughly before she swallows it the first time.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bò nuốt nhanh, không nhai nhiều lần đầu rồi mới nhai lại.

content.q: What lives in the rumen?
content.why: Đoạn 1: hàng tỷ vi khuẩn phân giải chất xơ.

content.q: What is chewing the cud?
opts: Bringing food back to the mouth to chew it again

content.q: What happens if a cow eats too much concentrate?
content.why: Đoạn 3: axit tích tụ trong dạ cỏ, bò có thể bệnh nặng.
opts: Acid builds up in the rumen.

content.q: How should a farmer change the diet?
content.why: Đoạn 3: thay đổi dần trong một đến hai tuần.
opts: Slowly, over a week or two

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Biosecurity on the farm
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Biosecurity means all the measures that stop diseases from entering or leaving a farm. Good biosecurity is cheaper than treating a disease outbreak, and it also protects public health.

The first rule is to control movements. Visitors must sign a book and wear clean boots and clothes. Vehicles are disinfected at the gate. New animals should be kept in quarantine for at least two weeks before they join the herd. During this time the farmer watches them for signs of illness and the vet takes blood samples.

The second rule is hygiene. Buildings and equipment are cleaned and disinfected regularly, and dead animals are removed quickly. Workers wash their hands and change their boots between different animal houses. Wild birds, rodents and insects can carry diseases, so farmers try to keep them out.

Finally, the farmer keeps good records. Each animal has an ear tag, and every treatment is written down. If an outbreak occurs, the records show where the disease came from and which animals are in danger. The vet visits regularly to check the vaccination programme and the health of the herd.

content.q: Good biosecurity is more expensive than treating an outbreak.
content.why: Đoạn 1: an toàn sinh học rẻ hơn xử lý dịch bệnh.

content.q: New animals should be kept in quarantine before joining the herd.
content.why: Đoạn 2: cách ly ít nhất hai tuần.

content.q: Workers change their boots between different animal houses.
content.why: Đoạn 3: rửa tay và thay ủng giữa các chuồng.

content.q: Farmers keep records only when animals are sick.
content.why: Đoạn 4: mỗi con có thẻ tai và mọi điều trị đều được ghi lại.

content.q: What happens to vehicles at the gate?
content.why: Đoạn 2: xe được khử trùng ở cổng.

content.q: How long should new animals stay in quarantine?
Why do records help in an outbreak?
content.why: Đoạn 4: ghi chép giúp truy nguồn bệnh và xác định đàn nguy cơ.
opts: They show where the disease came from and which animals are in danger.

content.q: What can carry diseases onto a farm?
content.why: Đoạn 3: chim hoang, loài gặm nhấm và côn trùng.

exercises.title: Bài 1 · Welfare: the five freedoms
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
Animal welfare means the physical and mental well-being of an animal. For many years, vets and scientists have used the five freedoms to explain what animals need. First, animals must be free from hunger and thirst, which means they have fresh water and a healthy diet. Second, they need freedom from discomfort, with a suitable shelter and a comfortable place to rest. Third, they must be free from pain, injury and disease. Fourth, they should be able to show normal behaviour, which requires enough space and company. Finally, they must be free from fear and distress.

Today, many experts say that welfare is not only about avoiding suffering. Animals should also have positive experiences, such as play and social contact. Environmental enrichment, for example toys for cats or straw for pigs, helps to achieve this.

Vets play an important role in welfare. They are often the first to notice neglect or cruelty, and in many countries they have a legal duty to report it. They also educate owners. A common problem is obesity: an overweight dog may develop joint pain and diabetes. Simple advice about diet and exercise can add years to its life.

content.q: The five freedoms include freedom from hunger and thirst.
content.why: Đoạn 1: tự do khỏi đói và khát.

content.q: Today, welfare is only about avoiding suffering.
content.why: Đoạn 2: động vật cũng cần trải nghiệm tích cực như chơi và giao tiếp.

content.q: Enrichment such as toys can improve welfare.
content.why: Đoạn 2: đồ chơi cho mèo, rơm cho heo.

content.q: Vets never notice neglect or cruelty.
content.why: Đoạn 3: bác sĩ thú y thường là người đầu tiên nhận ra.

content.q: What does the freedom to show normal behaviour require?
content.why: Đoạn 1: cần đủ không gian và bạn đồng loại.

content.q: What is an example of enrichment for pigs?
What problems can obesity cause in a dog?
content.why: Đoạn 3: đau khớp và tiểu đường.

content.q: What legal duty do vets often have?
content.why: Đoạn 3: ở nhiều nước có nghĩa vụ pháp lý báo cáo.

exercises.title: Bài 2 · Breaking bad news
exercises.instruction: Read the text and answer the questions.
exercises.instruction_vi: Đọc bài và trả lời câu hỏi (True = Đúng, False = Sai).
exercises.passage:
One of the hardest parts of a vet's job is talking to owners about serious illness or death. For many people, a pet is a member of the family, so the news can feel like losing a relative. Good communication does not remove the pain, but it can make the experience easier.

First, the vet chooses a quiet room and sits down with the owner. She speaks clearly and avoids technical words. Instead of using many medical terms, she explains the diagnosis simply and honestly. She then describes the options: treatment, palliative care or, if the animal is suffering and cannot be cured, euthanasia. The owner may want a second opinion, and the vet should respect this.

It is important to listen. The owner may cry or feel angry or guilty, and the vet should show empathy without hurrying. Costs should be explained honestly, and an estimate should be given before treatment. Finally, the vet gives written discharge instructions and arranges a follow-up call.

Many vets also feel sad after difficult cases. Talking to colleagues helps them to look after their own well-being.

content.q: Losing a pet can feel like losing a member of the family.
content.why: Đoạn 1: với nhiều người, thú cưng là thành viên gia đình.

content.q: The vet should use as many medical terms as possible.
content.why: Đoạn 2: nên tránh thuật ngữ và giải thích đơn giản.

content.q: Owners may want a second opinion.
content.why: Đoạn 2: bác sĩ cần tôn trọng nhu cầu này.

content.q: Vets never feel sad after difficult cases.
content.why: Đoạn 4: nhiều bác sĩ cũng buồn sau ca khó.

content.q: Where does the vet speak to the owner?
content.why: Đoạn 2: chọn phòng yên tĩnh và ngồi xuống.

content.q: Which option may be discussed if the animal is suffering and cannot be cured?
content.why: Đoạn 2: điều trị, chăm sóc giảm nhẹ hoặc an tử.

content.q: What should be given before treatment starts?
content.why: Đoạn 3: cần nêu chi phí trung thực và báo giá trước.

content.q: What helps vets look after their own well-being?
content.why: Đoạn 4: trao đổi với đồng nghiệp.
